# FINAL REPORT - SIH26113 Maternity Assist Belt

> **NOT A MEDICAL DEVICE.** Prototype for engineering evaluation. The ECG channel is not isolated and the board carries no battery protection circuit. Read `REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION.md` items B1 and B2 before applying power.

## 1. What was created

A complete Autodesk EAGLE 9 / Fusion Electronics project for the SIH26113 Maternity Assist Belt carrier board: a component library with every pinout verified against the manufacturer's datasheet, a seven-sheet schematic, a placed and routed four-layer board, 12 renders drawn from those files, and 18 documents.

Everything is generated from one source model (`scripts/design.py`), so the library, schematic, board, netlist, GPIO table, BOM and reports cannot disagree with each other. The generators verify themselves: `generate_schematic.py` re-parses its own output and asserts the netlist matches the model exactly, and `generate_board.py` does the same for elements and signals.

## 3 & 4. Exact components and variants used

Every pinout below was read from the manufacturer's datasheet; the citation for each is in [`COMPONENT_VERIFICATION.md`](./COMPONENT_VERIFICATION.md).

| Ref | Exact part | Manufacturer | Package | Why this variant |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `U1` | **TP4056-42-SOP8-PP** | NanJing Top Power | `SOIC-8-N` | SOP-8 is hand-solderable and the datasheet gives R_PROG directly; charge set to 500 mA, not 1 A, because this footprint has no thermal land |
| `U2` | **AP2112K-3.3** | - | `SOT-23-5` | 600 mA guaranteed minimum against a 510 mA worst case, and an LDO rather than a switcher because the ECG front end is 20 mm away |
| `U3` | **ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R2** | Espressif Systems | `ESP32-S3-WROOM-1` | **-N8R2 is mandatory** - octal-PSRAM variants reserve IO35/36/37, which this design uses |
| `U4` | **TMP117AIDRVR** | Texas Instruments | `WSON-6-DRV0006B` | WSON (DRV) is the only variant in production; TI publish its land pattern |
| `U5` | **LSM6DSOXTR** | STMicroelectronics | `LGA-14L-2.5X3.0` | LGA-14, I2C mode 1, address 0x6A (SA0 to GND) |
| `U6` | **AS5600-ASOM** | ams-OSRAM | `SOIC-8-N` | SOIC-8 - by far the easiest fine-position sensor to assemble; address 0x36 is fixed, which forced the second I2C bus |
| `U7` | **AD8232ACPZ-R7** | Analog Devices | `LFCSP-20-4X4-P050` | **supply 2.0-3.5 V only**, so it is on 3V3 and never on VBAT |
| `U8` | **HX711** | Avia Semiconductor | `SOP-16-N` | SOP-16, ratiometric to AVDD so sharing the 3V3 rail costs nothing; RATE grounded for 10 Hz |
| `Q1`, `Q2` | AO3400A (or pin-compatible logic-level N-FET) | Alpha & Omega | `SOT-23-3` | V_GS(th) low enough for 3.3 V drive |
| `D5`-`D8` | 1N5819HW | generic | `SOD-123` | 40 V / 1 A Schottky for flyback and piezo clamping |
| `J1`, `J8` | S2B-PH-K-S / S4B-PH-K-S | JST | `JST-PH-2/4` | PCB hole ø0.7 +0.1 mm read from JST's own board-layout figure |

## 6. Important design assumptions

Full reasoning in [`DESIGN_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](./DESIGN_ASSUMPTIONS.md). The seven that **depart from the architecture diagram** are marked.

| # | Assumption / decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **[CHANGE]** No battery protection on the board - a protected cell/pack is required | DW01A + FS8205A pinouts could not be verified, and guessing on a lithium protection circuit is not acceptable |
| 2 | **[CHANGE]** Four layers, not two: signal / GND plane / 3V3 plane / signal | Measured: on two layers the router finished ~50 of 81 nets and the reachable copper split into disconnected regions. The AD8232 amplifies a sub-millivolt signal by 1100 and its datasheet asks for a ground plane |
| 3 | **[CHANGE]** Two I2C busses, not one | AS5600 and MAX17048 are **both fixed at 0x36**. The diagram's single bus cannot work |
| 4 | **[CHANGE]** MAX17048 replaced by a breakout header plus a VBAT divider | datasheet unreachable; see section 5 |
| 5 | **[CHANGE]** Two discrete LEDs instead of an RGB | an RGB needs 3 GPIOs (none spare) and an addressable one needs >= 3.5 V, which the 3V3 rail cannot supply |
| 6 | **[CHANGE]** microSD as a 6-way module header | no socket land pattern could be verified, and the diagram itself describes 'module headers' |
| 7 | **[CHANGE]** USB as a 4-way header, not a receptacle | no USB-C land pattern could be verified; a wrong receptacle makes the board unprogrammable |
| 8 | AD8232 on **3V3 only** | absolute maximum 3.5 V; VBAT reaches 4.2 V while charging |
| 9 | All 8 analog signals on **ADC1** (GPIO1-10) | ADC2 is unusable while the radio is active |
| 10 | **-N8R2 module mandatory** | octal-PSRAM variants reserve IO35/36/37 |
| 11 | One ground net, one continuous plane - **no AGND/DGND split** | 8 signals cross the analog/digital boundary; one bridge cannot serve them, and a track crossing a plane split is the very failure mode a split is meant to avoid |
| 12 | ECG pass band ~7-40 Hz, gain 1100 | the datasheet's motion-artefact configuration - a belt on a walking subject is not a resting patient. **A heart-rate channel, not diagnostic ECG** |
| 13 | Charge current 500 mA (`R1` = 2.4 k), not 1 A | halves the linear charger's dissipation; the SOP-8 footprint has no thermal land |
| 14 | FSR dividers 10 k | geometric mean of the 2 k-100 k band, so the output spans 0.30-2.75 V without clipping |
| 15 | Clearance beats completeness | where the router could only finish a net by breaking the clearance rule it leaves an airwire instead. An airwire is visible; a 0.05 mm gap is not |

## 7. ERC status

**PASS - 0 errors, 0 warnings.** `scripts/validate_erc.py`, 11 rule groups, run against the same model that generates the `.sch`. 167 parts, 84 nets, 420 pin connections, and every pin on exactly one net - no floating pins, no pin on two nets.

Declared exceptions, each with the datasheet sentence that justifies it, are in [`ERC_REPORT.md`](./ERC_REPORT.md).

> **Autodesk EAGLE / Fusion's own ERC: NOT EXECUTED - TOOL UNAVAILABLE.** No EAGLE installation existed where these files were produced. Running it is step 6 of the build guide, where the exceptions you should expect to approve are pre-listed.

## 8. DRC status

**Geometry is clean: 0 clearance, width, drill, placement, keep-out or board-edge violations.**

- **measured minimum copper clearance anywhere on the board: 0.130 mm** - the figure to quote to the fabricator
- minimum track 0.15 mm (fine-pitch escapes only), minimum drill 0.30 mm
- the 4 reported errors are all *unrouted nets*, not geometry faults - see section 13

> **Autodesk EAGLE / Fusion's own DRC: NOT EXECUTED - TOOL UNAVAILABLE**, and neither is its copper-pour computation. Every plane-net *pad* has its own dedicated via, so pad connectivity does not depend on the pour. Build guide steps 14-15.

Rules, per-layer minima and every finding: [`DRC_REPORT.md`](./DRC_REPORT.md).

**100 x 70 mm** (70 cm2), 1.6 mm FR-4.

Mounting holes: 4 x M2 at (3, 3), (97, 3), (2.6, 42), (97, 67) - note `H3` is mid-left-edge rather than a corner, because the top-left corner falls inside the antenna keep-out.

## 12. Layer count

**4 copper layers**, EAGLE layer setup `(1*2*15*16)`.

| Layer | Role |
|---|---|
| 1 (`Top`) | signal + components |
| 2 (`Route2`) | GND plane (solid) |
| 15 (`Route15`) | 3V3 plane (solid) |
| 16 (`Bottom`) | signal |

Both plane polygons are drawn as an **L** that omits the antenna corner: Espressif require no copper - planes included - beneath the module antenna, and an EAGLE polygon cannot carry a hole.

## 13. Important risks

Ordered by consequence.

| Risk | Consequence if ignored | Mitigation / where it is recorded |
|---|---|---|
| **No battery protection on the board** | an unprotected Li-Po can vent or burn on over-charge or short | a cell/pack with an integrated protection module is **mandatory** at `J1`. `REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION.md` **B1** |
| **ECG is not isolated** | a subject is galvanically connected through 330 kOhm; with USB plugged into a mains supply that reference is the supply's secondary | battery power with USB disconnected whenever electrodes are attached; bench use with informed participants only. **B2** |
| **JST battery polarity is not standardised** | reverse-connecting the cell | `J1` pin 1 = `VBAT`(+), pin 2 = `GND`(-). Check with a meter before the first connection. **B1** |
| **Motor may be over-volted** | a 3.0 V coin motor on a 4.2 V cell will not last | `R45` (0 R, 0805) is in series so a ballast can be fitted without cutting tracks. **B3** |
| **Wrong module variant** | N8R8/N16R8 short the ECG leads-off and shutdown signals into the PSRAM bus | **-N8R2 only**. **H5** |
| **LDO dropout at low battery** | the 3V3 rail falls below the ESP32's 3.0 V minimum near the end of discharge, giving unpredictable brown-outs in a device with an SOS button | firmware **must** cut off at 3.5 V using `VBAT_SENSE` on `IO9` (1.75 V at the pin). `POWER_BUDGET.md` |
| **Fab clearance capability** | the fine-pitch fan-outs fail at the common 6 mil default | requires **5 mil / 0.127 mm**, which is usually a non-default option. **H6** |
| **Three parts need reflow** | AD8232, LSM6DSOX and TMP117 cannot be soldered with an iron | order a stencil with the boards. `BOM.md` |
| **TP4056 has no power-path switching** | load current flows through the charger and disturbs C/10 termination | accepted for a prototype; a production build should use MCP73871 or BQ24075. `DESIGN_ASSUMPTIONS.md` 1.3 |
| **TMP117 measures pod temperature, not skin** | the temperature channel is close to meaningless as placed | move it to a flex tail against the skin; the sensor bus is already on `J4`. **M7** |
| **Six of eight transducers are unselected** | `R37` in particular is a placeholder that will be wrong | project-planning gap rather than a board gap. **H2, H3, M3, M4** |
| **Pour geometry not computed** | a GND pad could in principle sit on an orphaned pour island | every plane-net pad has its own dedicated via, so connectivity does not rely on the pour. Confirm with `RATSNEST`. Build guide step 14 |

## 14. What needs to be verified physically

Nothing in this project is a measurement. Every figure is a datasheet value or a calculation.

| Verify | How | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 3V3 rail | `TP2` vs `TP3` with 5 V on `J2` | 3.3 V +/-1.5 % |
| Charge current | series meter into `J1` | ~500 mA in constant current, `D1` lit |
| Battery sense scaling | `IO9` reading vs a meter on `TP1` | pin = VBAT/2, so 4.2 V -> 2.10 V |
| Brown-out threshold | discharge and watch the 3V3 rail | rail sags below 3.0 V at roughly 3.3 V of cell |
| I2C bus scan | scan both busses | **0x48 and 0x6A** on the sensor bus; **0x36** on the angle bus |
| Part orientation | if a device is missing from the scan | the LSM6DSOX is the usual suspect - pin 1 is top-RIGHT in the footprint |
| ECG reference | `TP11` (`ECG_REFOUT`) after 2.5 s | ~1.65 V static |
| ECG output | `TP10` on a scope, electrodes off | idles near 1.65 V; `LOD+`/`LOD-` both high |
| ECG gain and band | inject a known 1 mV, 10 Hz differential signal | ~1.1 V pk-pk out; -3 dB near 7 Hz and 40 Hz |
| Mains rejection | run on battery near mains wiring | 50/60 Hz residual should be small; RLD gives ~26 dB |
| Load-cell channel | press the cell | HX711 reading changes monotonically |
| FSR range | press each FSR | 0.30 V unloaded to ~2.75 V at full force, no clipping |
| Piezo clamp | tap the film hard | `IO2` stays within 0 - 3.3 V |
| FET fail-safe | power up with motor and buzzer fitted | neither runs at boot |
| Strapping pins | power up with both LEDs fitted | boots normally into SPI boot |
| Radio range | with the battery in its final position | keep the pack >= 10 mm from the antenna |
| Enclosure fit | against `renders/pcb_3d.png` | tallest part 8.5 mm; heights marked *typical* need confirming |

## 15. Exact next steps in Autodesk Fusion

The full 20-step walkthrough is in [`PCB_BUILD_GUIDE.md`](./PCB_BUILD_GUIDE.md). The short version:

1. `Library > Open Library Manager > Import` `libraries/SIH26113_Maternity_Assist_Belt.lbr`, mark it **In Use**. (The `.sch` and `.brd` also embed a full copy, so they open without this - it is only needed to place *new* parts.)
2. Open `schematic/SIH26113_Maternity_Assist_Belt.sch`. Confirm 7 sheets and that every pin carries a green net label on a short stub. Connections are made by **named labels**, not long wires.
3. Spot-check four footprints against the datasheet pages cited in `COMPONENT_VERIFICATION.md`: `ESP32-S3-WROOM-1` (pin 1 is 7.49 mm below the antenna edge), `AD8232`, **`LSM6DSOX` (pin 1 is top-RIGHT - this is the classic mirror error)**, `TMP117`.
4. `Tools > ERC`. Approve only the exceptions pre-listed in build guide step 6; investigate anything else.
5. Switch to the `PCB` tab and **type `RATSNEST` immediately** - that is what makes Fusion compute the copper pours. Nothing looks right until you do.
6. Confirm the layer setup is `(1*2*15*16)` and that layer 2 holds one GND polygon and layer 15 one 3V3 polygon, both stopping short of the antenna corner.
7. Turn on layer 19 (`Unrouted`) and finish the **4 airwires** with the interactive router. Set the grid to 0.05 mm, enable 45 degree routing, and start from the end of each pad's existing fan-out stub rather than from the pad. Use the bottom layer freely - it is emptier, and both signal layers sit against a plane.
8. `Tools > DRC`. The board carries its own rule set (`SIH26113_4layer`). Fix anything it reports beyond the airwires.
9. `RATSNEST` again, then check on layer 2 that the GND plane under the ECG block is unbroken - that is the single most important electrical property of this board.
10. `PCB > 3D PCB` for a look. Remember **no STEP models are attached**, so this is not a real interference check; use `renders/pcb_3d.png` and the height table for the enclosure.
11. `Manufacturing > CAM Processor`, a 4-layer Gerber X2 job. You need the **top paste** layer too - order a stencil.
12. Tell the fab: 4 layers, 1.6 mm FR-4, 1 oz copper, **5 mil / 0.127 mm trace and gap**, 0.30 mm minimum drill, layers 2 and 15 are planes.
13. Before ordering, close the BLOCKING items in `REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION.md` (protected cell, ECG safety protocol, motor rating) and confirm the module is **-N8R2**.

Bring-up order once boards arrive is in the build guide: power only, then the module, then I2C, then mechanical sensing, then alerts, and **ECG last** - on battery, USB disconnected.

### The airwires, and why they are airwires

These are not routing failures. In each case the router could *only* finish the net by coming closer than the clearance rule, so it ripped the net out and left an airwire instead. An airwire is visible in Fusion the moment the board opens and is a minute's work to route by hand; a sub-rule gap is invisible and might reach fabrication.

| Net | Closest approach it would have needed | To | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| `I2C_SDA` | 0.075 mm | `FSR1_ADC` | 1 |
| `SD_CS` | 0.090 mm | `LED_ALERT` | 1 |
| `SD_MISO` | 0.145 mm | `ESP_EN` | 1 |
| `ESP_EN` | 0.145 mm | `PIEZO_ADC` | 1 |
